one_line: Lets an agent place and complete phone calls for errands.
what_it_does: A private judging web app where a user or agent describes a phone task and JooVoice places the call.
leverage_rationale: Phone calls completed through a structured agent surface are materially more reliable than a general agent clicking a UI, though the packet provides no end-to-end demonstration.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT TEXT says the agent can place calls and see them through to the end.
ABOUT TEXT describes both agent control and a human click-through path.
execution_rationale: The claimed workflow is coherent, but there are no submitted video frames or transcript and only packaging/demo-alive metadata, so execution cannot be strongly credited.
execution_evidence: demo_link=True and demo_alive=alive in FACTS.
No video or frame sheets submitted.
impact_rationale: Errand phone calls are a concrete, high-friction task with a clear audience of people who want assistants to transact by voice.
impact_evidence: PITCH and ABOUT TEXT identify making calls for errands as the core use case.
creativity_rationale: Combining an agent with live phone-call completion is a fresh and memorable application, even though voice agents are an established category.
creativity_evidence: ABOUT TEXT positions the product around agents carrying calls through to completion.
usability_note: Promised fast path after login, but no visual workflow evidence available.
standouts: Concrete agent-mediated phone action rather than text-only assistance.

one_line: A shared 3D studio for humans and agents to build and test physical machines.
what_it_does: Imports component evidence, assembles hardware in 3D, validates wiring, and runs deterministic physics experiments with shared agent-human state.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates on structured assemblies, evidence, topology, camera state, and simulations in the same live workspace; this is substantially beyond reliable generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT TEXT lists structured tools for loading examples, arranging components, validating connections, controlling the 3D view, and running experiments.
ABOUT TEXT explicitly states both collaborators share project state.
execution_rationale: The scope is ambitious and internally coherent, with a credible complete studio workflow and three submitted frame sheets, though exact end-to-end details remain partially unobservable from the text packet.
execution_evidence: FACTS report a live demo, public repository, and three frame sheets.
ABOUT TEXT describes import, assembly, wiring validation, simulation, telemetry, and findings.
impact_rationale: Hardware engineers and makers have a real problem: scattered specifications and the risk of building physically infeasible machines; the product directly targets that gap.
impact_evidence: ABOUT TEXT identifies incompatible batteries, underpowered motors, wiring, units, and evidence provenance as concrete problems.
Workflow addresses sourcing, validation, and simulation.
creativity_rationale: The combination of evidence-backed hardware modeling, shared agent-human 3D state, and deterministic physical experiments is unusually ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: ABOUT TEXT frames the product as an AI collaborator for real machine construction, not a black-box simulator.
Evidence status is preserved separately from provisional suggestions.
usability_note: A coherent studio is described; dense hardware workflows may still carry substantial learning cost.
red_flags: No transcript; frame-sheet visual details are not reliably available in this review due to vision service limits.
standouts: Shared live 3D state between human and agent.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP leverage, ambitious original concept, and substantial claimed product scope with supporting frame sheets and a live demo.

one_line: A consent and audit layer for risky WebMCP tool calls.
what_it_does: Adds metadata-driven approval, audit logging, attention cues, and optional WebAuthn gating to WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central: the package changes how agents are authorized and how tool state is governed, rather than merely exposing UI actions.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT TEXT describes a hook/provider integrated with @mcp-b/react-webmcp.
Risk, reversibility, scope, approval, and audit are attached to tool registration.
execution_rationale: The package concept is coherent and covers selective consent, logging, cross-tab cues, and biometric escalation; live demo and frame sheets support a strong claimed implementation.
execution_evidence: FACTS report public repo and live demo plus three frame sheets.
ABOUT TEXT specifies approved, denied, and auto-approved audit states.
impact_rationale: Any agent-enabled application needs a credible boundary for consequential actions; this addresses a broad and concrete safety/usability problem.
impact_evidence: ABOUT TEXT contrasts silent execution with selective approval for irreversible production actions.
Audit history and WebAuthn address accountability and high-risk operations.
creativity_rationale: Consent middleware is a strong synthesis of WebMCP, risk metadata, and WebAuthn, though approval systems themselves are an established pattern.
creativity_evidence: Cross-tab attention cues and per-tool reversibility metadata extend ordinary confirmation dialogs.
usability_note: Selective interruption and explicit risk communication are well aligned with agent workflows.
red_flags: No transcript; visual frame details unavailable because vision service was rate-limited.
advance_reason: High practical impact and strong WebMCP-native safety leverage with coherent claimed implementation.

one_line: A bank payment desk that grants agents bounded, revocable authority.
what_it_does: Lets agents investigate payments freely, then requires a human-edited mandate before dynamically exposing release and revoke tools.
leverage_rationale: Dynamic tool registration and revocation encode live authority boundaries that a general UI-driving agent cannot comparably and reliably reproduce.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT TEXT says release_under_mandate and revoke_mandate appear only after approval and vanish on revocation.
Mandates specify amount, total, rail, beneficiary, and duration.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete, carefully bounded workflow with explicit state transitions and a live demo, repository, gallery, and frame sheets.
execution_evidence: FACTS report live demo, public repo, five gallery images, and three frame sheets.
ABOUT TEXT covers investigate, propose, edit, grant, release, revoke, and dynamic tool-surface transitions.
impact_rationale: It targets a real high-consequence gap: useful agent investigation without unrestricted ability to move money.
impact_evidence: ABOUT TEXT articulates the binary credentials-or-nothing problem in payment operations.
Human-editable ceilings and immediate revocation directly mitigate consequential risk.
creativity_rationale: Treating agent authority as a negotiated, time-bounded, dynamically changing tool surface is a novel interaction model pursued deeply.
creativity_evidence: Mandate negotiation and tools appearing/disappearing mid-session are distinctive design choices.
usability_note: Explicit authority cards and revocation are understandable, though payment policy is inherently complex.
red_flags: Simulation rather than real banking execution should not be mistaken for production validation.
standouts: Clear human/agent boundary for money movement.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and impact with a deeply coherent, safety-conscious workflow.

one_line: A shared calendar agent that proposes conflict-aware plans while preserving human approval.
what_it_does: Inspects scoped availability and preferences, ranks options, stages bounded changes, and requires a reviewed diff before applying calendar mutations.
leverage_rationale: Structured availability, privacy-preserving busy blocks, bounded drafts, revision checks, confirmations, and idempotency make agent planning materially more reliable than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT TEXT lists scoped WebMCP inspection, weekly checks, bounded rescheduling, and reviewed change sets.
Apply path requires revision, one-time confirmation, and idempotency key.
execution_rationale: The central workflow is detailed and coherent, with live demo, public repository, and frame sheets; claimed scope includes both planning and safe application boundaries.
execution_evidence: FACTS report live demo, public repo, and three frame sheets.
ABOUT TEXT specifies before/after diff and no-notification draft behavior.
impact_rationale: Scheduling across distributed teams and household-like constraints is a common, real coordination problem, and privacy-preserving proposals offer credible value.
impact_evidence: ABOUT TEXT identifies time zones, focus time, travel buffers, work patterns, and conflicts.
Private events remain generic Busy blocks outside owner access.
creativity_rationale: Calendar assistants are familiar, but the bounded change-set, privacy model, and human-owned final decision provide a fresh interaction refinement.
creativity_evidence: One-instance rescheduling and reviewed revision/idempotency safeguards are unusually specific.
usability_note: Diff-based review and explicit confirmation support understandable, safe operation.
red_flags: No transcript; frame-sheet content could not be visually inspected due to service limits.
standouts: Safe staged mutations instead of broad write access.
advance_reason: Strong agent-native workflow with credible utility and careful mutation boundaries.

one_line: Turns broken contractual promises into reviewed enforcement actions.
what_it_does: Inspects a clause, computes a simulated remedy, drafts an enforceable demand, and files a simulated dispute after authorization.
leverage_rationale: Structured contract-to-entitlement-to-action state and explicit authorization make consequential enforcement more reliable than generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT TEXT defines four dedicated tools spanning clause inspection through filing.
Human authorization is required immediately before notice generation and filing.
execution_rationale: The packet presents one complete workflow with clear states and live/public evidence, though the action is explicitly simulated.
execution_evidence: FACTS report live demo, public repo, two gallery images, and three frame sheets.
ABOUT TEXT gives a concrete overdue invoice scenario and receipt-producing flow.
impact_rationale: People owed money or performance under contracts face real procedural friction; automating investigation and preparation while preserving final approval is credible value.
impact_evidence: ABOUT TEXT names clause finding, breach verification, remedy calculation, notice, filing, and evidence retention.
creativity_rationale: The contract-enforcement action pipeline is a distinctive agent use case, with a meaningful human-authority boundary.
creativity_evidence: Contract → Entitlement → Approval → Action → Receipt is a memorable end-to-end interaction model.
usability_note: Clear staged workflow, but legal concepts and simulated filing may be intimidating.
red_flags: Filing is simulated, so real-world legal reliability is not demonstrated.
standouts: Useful separation of preparation from consequential authorization.
advance_reason: Distinctive, credible workflow with strong impact and agent leverage despite simulation limits.

leverage_rationale: Structured fleet state, dependency maps, hypotheses, authorization, remediation transitions, and measured verification are central; generic UI driving would be markedly less dependable.

impact_rationale: Incident response is a high-value operational problem where faster diagnosis and governed remediation can materially reduce outages and risk.
impact_evidence: ABOUT TEXT describes latency/502 incident investigation across telemetry, logs, dependencies, changes, and constraints.

creativity_rationale: The governed collaborative command environment is a strong synthesis of agent investigation, human authorization, and operational evidence.

one_line: A household relocation map that solves and negotiates competing constraints.
what_it_does: Intersects commute, school, amenity, terrain, and health constraints over a real-city grid, then lets human edits synchronize with agent state and 3D terrain verification.
leverage_rationale: The shared solver state lets an agent parse constraints and a human adjust tradeoffs live, with immediate geometric updates; generic UI driving would be substantially less precise and repeatable.
leverage_evidence: VIDEO TRANSCRIPT describes agent-registered profiles, on-device intersection, synchronized slider edits, and dynamic polygon updates.
ABOUT TEXT describes concession sweeps and paired conflicting requirements.
execution_rationale: This is the best evidenced packet: a 184-second video transcript covers setup, constraint solving, manual intervention, synchronization, and 3D verification, alongside live demo and frame sheets.
execution_evidence: FACTS report live demo, video 184 seconds, four gallery images, and three frame sheets.
TRANSCRIPT gives concrete computed areas: 29.38, 13.44, and 11.88 square kilometers.
impact_rationale: Families relocating face a real multi-person constraint problem, and the product offers actionable compromise discovery rather than simplistic property filtering.
impact_evidence: TRANSCRIPT and ABOUT TEXT describe household members, schools, commute, injury, terrain, and negotiating concessions.

creativity_rationale: Constraint negotiation that exposes which human requirement must bend, combining map geometry with social/medical context, is original and memorable.
creativity_evidence: ABOUT TEXT emphasizes that ‘nowhere works’ becomes useful through smallest-concession analysis.
VIDEO TRANSCRIPT shows human and agent jointly changing constraints.
usability_note: Sliders, candidate zones, and 3D verification make complex tradeoffs legible.
standouts: Human judgment is preserved for value-laden compromises.
Concrete geometric treatment of household negotiation.
advance_reason: Exceptional evidence-backed execution, strong impact, and a distinctive shared human-agent interaction.

one_line: An agent-assisted spaced-repetition study system that grades explanations and schedules review.
what_it_does: Builds or selects validated decks, prompts recall in the learner’s own words, gets agent feedback, and records FSRS grades through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent a structured path to persist grades and update scheduling while the human supplies recall; the same outcome is possible otherwise but with meaningful integration friction.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT TEXT says the agent sends grades through WebMCP, which saves them and updates FSRS scheduling.
Validator and card rubrics provide structured state for agent teaching and grading.
execution_rationale: The study loop, validator, grading scale, scheduling, and feedback are coherent and supported by a live demo, twelve gallery images, and frame sheets, though no transcript is provided.
execution_evidence: FACTS report live demo, twelve gallery images, and three frame sheets.
ABOUT TEXT describes deck validation, recall, grading, definition reveal, feedback, and next-card progression.
impact_rationale: Learners have a clear problem—study systems impose setup and unreliable self-grading—and this directly supports retrieval practice and timely review.
impact_evidence: ABOUT TEXT explains deck setup and self-grading burdens.
FSRS scheduling and own-words recall address durable learning.
creativity_rationale: It is a thoughtful synthesis of spaced repetition and conversational agent feedback, with a meaningful reduction of study setup burden, though the category is established.
creativity_evidence: Agent-built decks plus rubric-based grading in the study loop are a substantive interaction angle.
usability_note: One clear study loop and familiar Again/Hard/Good/Easy controls suggest good usability.
red_flags: Validator cannot verify every factual claim, as acknowledged in ABOUT TEXT.
standouts: Preserves learner effort while removing setup and self-grading burden.
advance_reason: Clear audience need, coherent learning loop, and meaningful WebMCP integration with strong supporting packaging.
